issues.source_quote: Чтоб ты исдох! Чтоб я видел тебя у гробу, у белых тапках! Чтоб ты жил на одну зарплату!
issues.translation_quote: Drop dead! I hope to see you in your coffin, in your white funeral slippers! May you have to live on nothing but your wages!
issues.justification: The neighbor's curse is in a dialectal, Odessa-flavored voice (у гробу, у белых тапках); the English is standard and loses the character's comic voice. The wage curse is also flattened.
Loss of dialect and comedic over-the-top Odessa curse style.

issues.source_quote: Лёлик, на его месте должен быть я. Напьёшься - будешь!
issues.translation_quote: Boys, I should be the one lying there. Get drunk and you will be!
issues.justification: The scene is a street drunk joke; 'Ребята' mistranslated as 'Boys' and the joke about the drunk lying on the ground is weakened.

issues.source_quote: Кто возьмёт билетов пачку, тот получит... Водокачку!
issues.translation_quote: Buy a whole book of tickets and you might just win... A water pump!
issues.justification: The rhyming pitch (пачку/водокачку) is a comic doggerel; the English loses the rhyme and humor.
'Closed fracture' is rendered as 'simple fracture', and the later 'открытый перелом' as 'compound fracture'; the Nadya joke works but 'simple' loses the clear closed/open contrast.

The recurring running gag of the boss's cynical aphorisms (often garbled: 'куй железо, не отходя от кассы') loses the mixed-proverb humor, as 'strike while the iron's hot' drops the cash register element.

issues.source_quote: Нет, на это я пойтить не могу!
issues.translation_quote: No, I can't agree to that!
issues.justification: Gorbunkov's mock-bureaucratic/folk 'пойтить' is flattened, losing comic voice.
